page.layout: One page of text: a running head at the top, a verse epigram in italic above, then a full-width title block, an elegy heading, and the verse of the elegy in roman below.

p.i: Implerunt Monachi defertis oppida sylvis, Quid magis est Sariis Satibus orbe frequens. Nocte dieque rudit Monachus, cantatque Poëta Et placet immodicè stultus Sterque sibi. Cuique sua est Sati lasciuo Cynthia frater Sape pius dominas quattuor snus habet. Friget carmen aqua potori infuane poëta, Triste canit pota frater anhelus aqua. Accinctus cithara resonat sua carmina Sates: Sic Monachi cingit plena lagena latus, Hunc [illegible, ~3 letters] furor exagitat, furorque [illegible, ~3 letters] illum: Ipse gerit thyrsos, & gerit ille cruces: Victores ornat laurus myrtúsve poëtas: Sunt Monachis tonsa sacra corona coma. Denique des Monacho Musas, Satiqueque cucullum Vates & Monachus fiet Sterque tibi.

main_text.head: IN FAMILIARVM ROMANARVM stemmata edita à generosissimo Domino, & tùm bonarum omnium literarum cognitione, tum virtutibus omnibus ornatissimo, Domino Richardo Strenio, Baroni Suarzenauio.
Elegia X.
main_text.p: VIctricis quòdam domitrix Germania Roma, Insolito pressit subdita colla iugo. Nec contenta ferox ferro strauisse Quiritesᵣ Per-

page.notes: The epigram's Greek words in the fifth and sixth lines are printed in Greek letters and could not be read with certainty, so they are marked illegible. The drop-cap V of the elegy is read as V. The last line "Per-" is a hyphenated line end, kept with its hyphen. The "Quiritesᵣ" mark at the line end is a printed mark that I could not confirm.
